A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SplashNet study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original emg2qwerty zero-shot and user-specific finetuning experiments, architectural ablations, and participant-level CER results (Tables 1–4 and Figure 4).

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original masking and normalization ablations, representation analyses, alternative participant splits, and emg2pose evaluations (Tables 5–10 and Figure 5).

M1.justification: The principal SplashNet architecture and preprocessing remain unchanged. Appendix A.9 adds an adaptation for emg2pose: RTN and ACM operate on first-convolution outputs, with ACM zeroing 50% or 75% of features in specified training samples. This changes the procedure for the added task.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only emg2qwerty typing; emg2pose is merely cited. v2 adds actual hand-pose tracking experiments under user, stage, and combined generalization regimes (Appendix A.9, Table 10), substantially extending the evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: The original typing comparisons retain Sivakumar et al. and the same model variants. v2 additionally evaluates the Salter et al. emg2pose baseline against adaptations using RTN, ACM, and their combination (Table 10).

E3.justification: v2 adds an 18-user training-domain beam-search evaluation and a separate 78/18 training/validation experiment retaining the original eight test users (Section 4.6, Appendix A.8). Added protocols also vary masking order, mask width, and normalization windows, and evaluate pose tracking with angular-error and landmark-distance metrics. These are additional experimental designs, not replacements of the original typing protocol.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component and decoding comparisons, v2 tests pre-aggregation masking, ACM widths, RSG removal, RTN window matching, and mean-imputation masking (Tables 5–8). It also adds UMAP representations and alternative-split analyses (Figure 5, Table 9), substantially expanding evidence about mechanisms and robustness.

E5.justification: Appendix A.5 introduces two-tailed paired tests for the new sensitivity analyses, while the main comparisons retain one-tailed tests. Tables 5 and 6 newly provide standard deviations for some previously reported greedy and other-domain results. Neither version discloses seed or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Original typing CERs remain unchanged, including SplashNet's 35.67% zero-shot and 5.51% finetuned results. However, Table 1 revises baseline/mini/full-model GFLOPs from 201.325/118.346/229.384 to 61.61/36.84/71.38 under the same stated 30-second measurement description. v2 also adds extensive validation, ablation, representation, and pose-tracking results; these are new results under specified conditions, not same-setting accuracy improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for spectral aggregation, RTN, masking, and encoder operations are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added analyses are empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding claims retain the same three principal contributions, compact-model efficiency claims, and approximately 31% zero-shot and 21% finetuned error reductions. The added experiments do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies low-order feature similarity as a working hypothesis (Section 2). New analyses develop interpretations concerning masking-value stability, matched normalization context, and the masking explanation for poorer greedy decoding. Appendix A.9 also identifies limited transfer to pose tracking and proposes early electrode mixing as a possible boundary, substantially extending the mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 documents implementation details for the added variants, including inverse spectral-mask mapping, mean imputation, and feature masking after the first emg2pose convolution. Figure 5 specifies activation sampling every 100th timestep from one session per test user. The original optimizer, schedule, hardware, runtime, and repository disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 3, the 22 cited works, and the Split-and-Share novelty positioning are unchanged. Salter et al. and emg2pose were already discussed in v1; their additional experimental use does not introduce a new literature positioning claim.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted wording corrections and explanatory additions, moves the beam-search description from Appendix A.5 into Section 4.5, and adds acknowledgments and a conference checklist. The main narrative and most existing prose remain intact; the scientific appendix additions do not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the empirical displays with Tables 5–10 and the four-panel UMAP Figure 5. Tables 1 and 3 gain training-domain columns and explanatory captions, with gray text distinguishing those results. Original Figures 1–4 are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses substantive evidential gaps in v1 through the masking-order control, normalization and masking sensitivity tests, and the alternative participant split (Tables 5–9). These strengthen assessment of the proposed mechanisms and generalization. Explicitly qualifying the low-order hypothesis and reporting weak pose-transfer gains also clarify applicability. Although the substantial FLOPs revision remains insufficiently explained, the added controls and more careful interpretation provide a substantial net quality improvement.
